preamble: Palatalization of the voiceless velar stop [k] to the voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate [tɕ] before front vowels and [j]. In Mandarin, Middle Chinese velars before high front vowels and medial -j- merged with the alveolar sibilants into the alveolo-palatal series written j/q/x in Pinyin, so that 家 Middle Chinese kae is Mandarin jiā [tɕi̯ä], while Cantonese keeps [k] (gaa1). The same outcome arose independently in Finland Swedish, where historical /k/ before front vowels is the affricate [tɕ] (Sweden Swedish has the fricative [ɕ]), and in Southern Gyeongsang Korean, where ki is pronounced [tɕi].

examples.note: Sweden Swedish /²ɕʏrka/ has a fricative; Finland Swedish keeps the affricate stage.
Dialectal palatalization of ki/ky to [tɕ] (Korean ㅈ), e.g. also 귤 "tangerine" > jul.

examples.to: [tɕ ~ cç], written ⟨ky⟩, e.g. kyerɛ 'to show', nkyene 'salt'
examples.note: Synchronic allophony: Wikipedia's allophone table gives /k/ as [k, tɕ~cç], and Dolphyne describes k as replaced by ky [ʨ] before front vowels in stem words. The rule continues a diachronic change, since all Akan palatal affricates go back to plain velars. Many words are exceptions (kete 'a dance', kisie 'rat'), and Adomako (2018) concludes the rule is no longer productive.

From Christaller's dictionary, via Adomako (2018): velar palatalization applies in the reduplicant before i. This is a rare case, because palatalization normally fails in reduplication (ka 'bite' → kɪ-ka).
